approvalRequirements: Purchase or lease a new eligible Class 2b through Class 8 battery-electric commercial vehicle for qualifying California operations.
Use a participating retailer and satisfy the customer, vehicle, registration, use, and claim-documentation rules.
For Class 2b vehicles, meet the additional public-fleet eligibility restriction.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current reward reduces the price of eligible commercial battery-electric vehicles; it does not fund EV charger installation, so the mapped retrofit is outside the program scope.
reviews.evidenceText: The current program is a point-of-sale reward for eligible new medium- and heavy-duty commercial battery-electric vehicles, not charging equipment.

approvalRequirements: Submit a complete ECAMS application by the active solicitation deadline.
Propose eligible publicly accessible high-powered DC fast-charging stations and satisfy site, equipment, corridor, utility, permitting, environmental, and readiness requirements.
Provide exactly 20 percent match for total allowable project cost, with at least half of the match in cash.
Pass administrative screening, technical scoring, and cost-per-CCS-port ranking within available funds.
Obtain California Energy Commission Business Meeting approval, execute the grant agreement, and receive required federal authorization before reimbursable work.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: GFO-25-603 is active but competitive. Applications are screened, scored, ranked, and funded only while the available appropriation lasts, with later approval and agreement gates.
reviews.evidenceText: The active solicitation offers up to 79 million dollars but uses competitive screening, scoring, cost ranking, match, formal approval, agreement, and federal-authorization requirements.

approvalRequirements: Apply during an active CALeVIP funding window for an eligible California DC fast-charging site.
Meet applicant, site-access, public-availability, equipment, networking, and program geography requirements.
Provide ready-to-build evidence such as an issued permit and final utility service design when required by the window.
Receive a funds-reserved notice, meet equipment-order and construction milestones, complete installation and inspections, and submit final disbursement documents.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Upcoming windows are limited to qualifying DC fast-charger projects and prioritize installation-ready sites. Funding is reserved only after application review and remains subject to available funds and milestones.
reviews.evidenceText: Current CALeVIP opportunities support DC fast-charger purchase and installation through defined application windows; window replacement is not an eligible measure.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible commercial, public, industrial, agricultural, or qualifying high-rise multifamily project in participating California investor-owned utility territory.
Be new construction or a qualifying major alteration rather than a stand-alone equipment replacement.
Engage the program early enough for whole-building energy and decarbonization design analysis.
Submit project information and complete the design-assistance and any related utility incentive verification process.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: CEDA is no-cost design assistance for eligible new construction and major alterations. An LED project can qualify only when it is part of a broader eligible design project, not merely because it is an LED retrofit.
reviews.evidenceText: CEDA evaluates eligible new construction and major-alteration projects during design and may identify utility incentives; it is not an automatic stand-alone lighting rebate.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible property in a jurisdiction where RenewPACE financing is currently available.
Use financing for a qualifying permanently affixed improvement, including eligible energy-storage work.
Pass property-based eligibility, payment-history, equity, ability-to-pay, and other underwriting requirements.
Complete required disclosures, consents, contractor documentation, and financing agreements before funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current successor offering is financing rather than a rebate. Approval depends on participating-area availability, project eligibility, property underwriting, disclosures, and execution of financing documents.
reviews.evidenceText: RenewPACE is property-based PACE financing subject to approval and underwriting; qualifying energy improvements may be financed only in participating areas.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible nonresidential SDG&E account, including qualifying bundled, direct-access, or community-choice service.
Enroll through an approved third-party aggregator or qualify and register as a self-aggregator.
Provide required enrollment documents and receive SDG&E eligibility confirmation.
Submit monthly capacity commitments, respond to dispatched events, and deliver verified load reduction.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: After approved enrollment, payments are operationally determined by monthly commitments and verified demand reduction. Controls can support performance, but the program does not award a hardware rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: The program approves eligible accounts or aggregators, accepts monthly capacity commitments, and pays for verified event performance.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible SCE general-service or agricultural account with required interval metering.
Enroll through a registered aggregator or obtain approval to self-aggregate.
Submit monthly load-reduction nominations and comply with event-notification and dispatch requirements.
Achieve verified load reduction for settlement under the tariff.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: CBP-E payments follow approved enrollment, monthly nominations, and measured performance. Automated demand-response controls may help deliver reductions but are not themselves the paid measure.
reviews.evidenceText: SCE permits aggregator or approved self-aggregator participation and bases capacity payments on nominated and verified load reduction.

approvalRequirements: Be a Cape Hatteras Electric Cooperative member with the charger installed at the member residence on Hatteras Island.
Install an eligible ChargePoint Level 2 charger with Wi-Fi connectivity.
Submit the rebate and data-sharing application with an itemized receipt and required account and device information.
Authorize the required charging-data access and satisfy program verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current member bill credit uses objective equipment, location, receipt, connectivity, and data-sharing requirements; a compliant claim is ordinarily awardable after review.
reviews.evidenceText: CHEC offers a member bill credit for an eligible ChargePoint Level 2 charger installed at a Hatteras Island residence after application and documentation review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Cape Light Compact business customer with a qualifying measure and utility account.
Use the applicable instant, prescriptive, or custom pathway for the selected equipment or building measure.
Obtain preapproval before installation where the measure or custom pathway requires it.
Submit specifications, invoices, calculations, and access for inspection or benefit-cost review as applicable.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Many mapped measures have current prescriptive or instant incentives, while larger or nonstandard projects use preapproval and cost-effectiveness review. Meeting the correct pathway generally produces an award.
reviews.evidenceText: Cape Light Compact provides business incentives through instant, prescriptive, and custom tracks, with preapproval or technical review required for specified measures.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible residential customer and property within Cape Light Compact program territory.
Purchase and install equipment or complete envelope work that meets current measure specifications.
Use approved or participating contractors and complete an assessment, weatherization, whole-home verification, or inspection where the selected measure requires it.
Submit the required claim, invoice, equipment, and installation documentation or receive the applicable instant incentive.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current residential incentives cover multiple mapped HVAC, water-heating, envelope, window, and appliance measures. Awards are generally objective once measure-specific verification and documents are complete.
reviews.evidenceText: Cape Light Compact lists current residential rebates and incentives with measure-specific contractor, assessment, product, verification, and claim requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Carbon Power and Light member-owner and install a currently listed qualifying product or measure.
Submit the program application within the stated post-purchase period, generally 90 days.
Provide invoices, proof of purchase, model or efficiency documentation, and other measure-specific records.
For EV charging, include the equipment and installation on one application and meet applicable electrical-code requirements.
Permit program inspection or additional verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The live utility rebate schedule uses defined equipment and documentation rules and credits approved incentives to the member account. Multiple mapped measures are currently listed.
reviews.evidenceText: Carbon Power and Light currently advertises energy-efficiency credits and publishes measure-specific incentives, documentation rules, and claim timing on its live member rebate page.

approvalRequirements: Use the current Carroll White REMC successor program rather than the former Carroll County REMC entity.
Install an eligible air-source or ground-source heat pump at a qualifying member residence.
Provide proof of purchase and complete the required post-installation inspection.
Confirm whether the contractor or member is the current rebate recipient.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Carroll County REMC no longer operates as a separate current program administrator. The successor utility has a contractor heat-pump rebate, but the legacy record and intended award recipient require reconciliation.
reviews.evidenceText: Carroll White REMC is the post-merger utility and currently pays a heat-pump incentive to contractors after proof of purchase and successful inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Carroll EMC member with the charger serving a residential account.
Purchase a new nonportable Level 2 charger certified by an accepted testing laboratory.
Submit the application and proof of purchase within 45 days of purchase.
Complete installation and pass Carroll EMC inspection before reimbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current 250-dollar member rebate has objective charger, timing, documentation, and inspection conditions. A compliant member claim is normally payable after approval.
reviews.evidenceText: Carroll EMC offers a residential Level 2 home-charger rebate after timely application, qualifying equipment verification, installation, and inspection.

approvalRequirements: Install an eligible air-source or ground-source heat pump at a Carroll White REMC member residence.
Use the current contractor rebate process.
Provide proof of purchase and pass the required post-installation inspection.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current successor utility states a fixed contractor rebate after proof of purchase and successful inspection, making payment likely when the stated requirements are met.
reviews.evidenceText: Carroll White REMC currently offers contractors a fixed incentive for qualifying air-source or ground-source heat-pump installations after inspection.

approvalRequirements: Be a Carteret-Craven Electric Cooperative member with an eligible residential service location.
Purchase and install a qualifying ENERGY STAR heat-pump water heater for the currently documented rebate.
Submit the application with a paid receipt and required equipment and account information.
Confirm current eligibility separately for mapped HVAC measures because the current official rebate page does not document those measures.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official rebate page clearly supports a heat-pump water-heater rebate, but it does not substantiate the two mapped HVAC rebate categories. The opportunity is only partially evidenced.
reviews.evidenceText: The current cooperative rebate page documents a 300-dollar qualifying heat-pump water-heater rebate and application requirements; current HVAC rebate evidence was not found.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying Washington commercial or industrial Cascade Natural Gas customer on an eligible rate schedule.
Install current qualifying high-efficiency natural-gas equipment, weatherization, or another listed measure in compliance with code.
Obtain project-specific review before installation for custom measures and provide estimated cost, project details, and savings calculations.
Submit the current application with account information, invoices, model data, and measure-specific documentation.
Permit inspection or verification before final payment when selected.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The 2026 commercial program lists prescriptive incentives and a custom path. Prescriptive claims are generally objective; custom projects require prior technical review and verified savings.
reviews.evidenceText: Cascade Natural Gas publishes current Washington commercial incentives, eligible rate schedules, documentation rules, code requirements, and custom-project review criteria.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Washington residential Cascade Natural Gas customer on the applicable service and rate schedule.
Use natural gas as the primary heat source where the selected measure requires it.
Install current qualifying equipment or building-envelope measures and use a licensed contractor where required.
Submit the completed application, invoices, and measure-specific documentation within the current claim period, generally 90 days after installation.
Permit inspection or verification when selected.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential program provides objective equipment and envelope rebates after customer, fuel, product, installation, and claim verification. ENERGY STAR certification alone is not a separate incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Cascade Natural Gas maintains current Washington residential rebate offerings with customer, equipment, installation, invoice, timing, and inspection conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Cedar Falls Utilities commercial customer for the utility service associated with the measure.
Install currently qualifying equipment and meet the applicable efficiency and contractor requirements.
Obtain CFU preapproval before installation for custom equipment or other measures identified as preapproval-required.
Provide approved calculations, specifications, invoices, and the completed rebate application by the current deadline.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: CFU allows some listed equipment to proceed without preapproval and requires preapproval for custom projects. Awards are generally likely after following the correct measure-specific path.
reviews.evidenceText: CFU publishes current commercial rebates and states that custom projects require preapproval, approved savings calculations, licensed work, and a complete claim.

approvalRequirements: Receive the applicable Cedar Falls Utilities service at the residential installation address.
Install a currently qualifying product or complete qualifying envelope work through a professional or licensed contractor where required.
Obtain preapproval before specified envelope or other preapproval-required work begins.
Provide itemized invoices, model and efficiency records, permits, test results, or AHRI documentation as required by the measure.
Submit the current rebate application by its stated deadline.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: CFU maintains current residential applications for numerous mapped HVAC, water-heating, envelope, window, and EV measures. Approval is measure-specific but generally objective once prerequisites are met.
reviews.evidenceText: CFU publishes current residential rebate forms with measure-specific preapproval, contractor, testing, product, invoice, and submission requirements.

approvalRequirements: Notify CFU Energy Services of intent to participate before the foundation inspection.
Construct an eligible single-family home using the required CFU utility services.
Meet all minimum code and program criteria and the full requirements of the selected ENERGY STAR, DOE Efficient New Homes, or Passive House tier.
Complete required inspections, rating, certification, and final application documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The 2026 Better Home Program provides defined tiered rebates and objective preconstruction, inspection, and certification conditions. A compliant enrolled project is likely to receive the stated tier payment.
reviews.evidenceText: CFU requires notification before foundation inspection and pays tiered new-home rebates after code compliance, program criteria, inspections, and certification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Cedarburg Light and Water commercial, industrial, or agricultural customer with a qualifying efficiency project.
Complete preproject technical review and establish projected energy and cost savings.
Receive financing approval while program capital is available and execute the shared-savings agreement.
Complete the project, provide invoices and a completion certificate, and satisfy savings or installation verification.
Repay the approved financing through the utility-bill mechanism.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a financing program with technical review, approval, agreement, and limited-capital constraints rather than an automatic rebate. Qualifying projects may receive up to the program financing limit.
reviews.evidenceText: The utility offers businesses upfront capital for qualifying energy-efficiency projects, subject to project review, agreement, completion, and repayment requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be a customer of a utility participating in Focus on Energy, including eligible Cedarburg Light and Water customers.
Purchase or install a current qualifying product or measure and meet the applicable efficiency specifications.
Use a participating contractor, distributor, or seller for measures delivered as instant discounts when required.
For mail-in rebates, submit the application, invoices, and technical records within the stated measure deadline.
Obtain income-qualified approval before installation when seeking an enhanced-income incentive.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current Focus on Energy residential incentives use published product, contractor, utility-participation, and claim rules. Eligible standard claims are normally awarded after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Cedarburg directs customers to current Focus on Energy residential rebates and discounts, which use participating-utility, product, contractor, and timely-claim requirements.

approvalRequirements: Use an approved project sponsor and register the project in CenterPoint Energy ETrack.
Locate the eligible commercial or industrial project in CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric territory and propose qualifying efficiency measures.
Submit the project application and secure a funding reservation before installation.
Execute the Standard Agreement and provide any required deposit or project documentation.
Install the measures, submit installation and savings reports, and pass inspection and verified kilowatt and kilowatt-hour savings review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The standard-offer process reserves limited incentive funds through approved sponsors before installation and pays against verified savings. Selection and payment are therefore project- and budget-dependent.
reviews.evidenceText: CenterPoint Energy requires sponsor registration, a preinstallation project application and agreement, installation reporting, inspection, and verified demand and energy savings before payment.

approvalRequirements: Have an eligible home in CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric territory.
Receive the retrofit through a participating approved contractor or program sponsor because incentives are paid to sponsors rather than directly to customers.
Install measures that meet the current program specifications and allow pre- and post-installation verification.
For the hard-to-reach pathway, document the applicable household-income or other qualifying status.
Complete customer acknowledgments and provide site access and supporting records required by the sponsor and utility.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The utility delivers incentives through approved contractors and sponsors using verified savings and limited program budgets. Customer participation may be subsidized, but an award is not a direct automatic customer rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: CenterPoint Energy residential and hard-to-reach incentives are implemented by approved sponsors, with qualifying measures, customer eligibility, and verified savings required.

approvalRequirements: Have the applicable CenterPoint Energy Indiana gas or electric service for the selected measure.
Purchase and install equipment or envelope work that meets current efficiency and product requirements.
Use an approved contractor for measures that require one, including specified attic-insulation and duct work.
Submit the rebate application, itemized invoice, and technical documentation, or obtain the incentive through a participating instant-discount channel.
Complete the transaction within the current program period and while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Indiana program publishes standard rebates and instant discounts for several mapped HVAC, water-heating, thermostat, insulation, window, and appliance measures. Compliant claims are generally awardable.
reviews.evidenceText: CenterPoint Energy Indiana lists current home-improvement rebates and discounts with service, equipment, contractor, invoice, and application requirements.
